about: reelkit.fx.Particles: what emit makes, alive, _pos and draw
note: args.canvas makes the picture, w x h x 3: bytes first (with only "flat", that colour everywhere; with "mul" and "add", pixel i, counted row by row from the top left, has the channels (mul[c] * i + add[c]) % 256), then, in float64, byte * gain + bias (when "gain" is there; both float.hex()), then the cast to "dtype" (float32 or float64). The result: expect.returned is "img" when Python returned the very array it was given (in place, or untouched) and "new" when it made one; expect.dtype is the dtype of what came back. The picture is stored as its difference from a baseline: expect.baseline is "canvas" (the picture as made) or "bytes" (np.clip(canvas, 0, 255).astype(np.uint8), which is what a drawing call that draws starts from; one that draws nothing returns the picture itself, and its baseline is "canvas"); expect.box [x0, y0, x1, y1] bounds the pixels that differ from the baseline (null: none do) and "out" is that part of the result, stored as uint8 when every value in it is a whole number from 0 to 255 (expect.stored says which dtype). Outside the box the result equals the baseline. args.cam holds a reelkit.camera.Cam by its fields: pos, M (rows right, up, fwd), f, cx, cy, near, target. "Particles(seed, max_alive) after the script": the arrays are the columns of _arrays() (sorted by t0, stably), by name; p, v and col are (n, 3); shape, tn are int64, ground and glow bool. alive(t): per time of "t", "count" indices into those columns, one after another in "idx". _pos: for the particles alive at t, at their ages u = t - t0: out (k, 3). draw(img, cam, t, light): args.light is null or names a Flares script and a time; the light is then lambda P: 1.0 + gain * FL.tint(P, t), as kit.picture passes it.
